facts.text: Statistics are the binding constraint on demonstrating collision-mitigation performance.

facts.text: Demonstrating a miss rate of at most 1% at 95% confidence with zero misses requires 299 independent trials per population.

Showing fewer than one unnecessary brake per 100 hours requires 300 representative operating hours with no unnecessary brakes.

facts.text: The statistical unit of analysis for collision-mitigation testing is the independent encounter, not individual frames.
facts.quote: Frames are not trials; the unit of analysis is the independent encounter.

facts.text: Across 100 or more site types, 10 or more scenarios, several conditions and many machine models, the testing strata exceed 7,000 cells.

facts.text: Collision-mitigation campaigns must keep three classes separate: discovery tests that try to break the system, a frozen and pre-registered estimation sample measuring how often the system succeeds, and regression tests checking whether changes broke required behavior.
facts.quote: Three campaign classes must be kept apart

facts.text: The failure fraction from a discovery campaign must never be reported as a field failure rate.

facts.text: The audit set for collision-mitigation testing must never become another tuning set.

facts.text: Collision-mitigation tuning is a constrained multi-objective problem: missed or late interventions are a hard constraint, while false warnings, unnecessary brakes and productivity loss are optimized with the Pareto front kept visible.
facts.quote: Tuning is a constrained multi-objective problem: missed or late interventions as a hard constraint, then false warnings, unnecessary brakes and productivity loss optimized with the Pareto front kept visible.

facts.text: Over-fitting in collision-mitigation tuning is avoided through grouped splits that hold out whole sites, weather episodes and machine models, together with a frozen test set.
facts.quote: Over-fitting is avoided with grouped splits (whole sites, weather episodes, machine models held out) and a frozen test set.

facts.text: Collision-mitigation settings should transfer across machine models through physics rather than copied constants: expressing zones as functions of speed, latency, braking deceleration, sensor pose and machine envelope turns per-model tuning into per-model measurement.
